sustainability.description: The feature's long-term environmental and resource impact across compute, storage, energy, and lifecycle effects.

rubric.pass: Resource use is bounded and proportionate to the value delivered. Lifecycle impact (storage retention, compute footprint, hardware demand) is documented or measurable.
rubric.fail: The feature creates substantial unbounded resource consumption, or relies on practices known to be environmentally harmful, with no mitigations.
rubric.borderline: Resource impact is unclear, only partially mitigated, or relies on assumptions that have not been validated.

scoring_notes: Consider compute, storage, network, and lifecycle effects together — not just runtime cost.
Be conservative when telemetry or actual measurements are missing.
A feature that scales linearly with users without bounded retention is rarely sustainable.
Default settings carry the most weight; an opt-in efficient mode does not redeem a wasteful default.

accessibility.description: Equitable usability across abilities, devices, languages, and contexts of use.

rubric.pass: Primary user flows meet WCAG 2.2 AA where applicable, work with keyboard-only and screen-reader navigation, and degrade gracefully on low-bandwidth or older devices.
rubric.fail: The feature systematically excludes users with common assistive needs, low-bandwidth contexts, or non-default device classes.
rubric.borderline: Partial coverage; key flows have not been tested against assistive technology, or accessibility is acknowledged but not enforced.

scoring_notes: Assess against WCAG 2.2 AA where applicable; do not require AAA unless the domain demands it.
Consider non-visual and motor disabilities, not only visual.
Mobile, low-bandwidth, and older devices are part of accessibility, not separate concerns.
